life_summary: Sylvester Quayle Cannon was born on June 10, 1877, in Salt Lake City, Utah Territory, as the son of apostle George Q. Cannon. He received advanced technical education, earning a degree in mining engineering from MIT and studying at the University of Utah. Cannon pursued a professional career in mining and engineering, applying his technical expertise to Church business interests and community development in Utah. His intellectual rigor and administrative acumen made him a natural fit for leadership roles. He married and established a family while maintaining his professional responsibilities in the growing Utah economy.
church_summary: Cannon began his missionary service in Belgium in 1899 and became president of the Netherlands–Belgium Mission from 1900 to 1902. He also accompanied apostle Francis M. Lyman on a significant three-month journey through the Mediterranean and Middle East. Cannon served as Presiding Bishop of the LDS Church from 1925 to 1938, providing administrative oversight of Church welfare and temporal affairs. He was ordained as an apostle in 1938, initially holding the unique status of an associate member of the Quorum of the Twelve before becoming a full member in 1939. He served in the Quorum until his death in 1943.
